newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: France plays down French Guiana riots.
newsitem.headline: France plays down French Guiana riots.

text.p: France on Thursday played down overnight riots in French Guiana ignited by the detention of three members of the territory's independence movement.

Nine police were injured in the riots but Dominique Vian, French government representative (Prefect) in France's South American department, said that though the violence was ferocious it did not constitute an insurrection.
"The situation is not an insurrection, we are far from that," Vian told a news conference. "I hear rumours that we (France) are on the verge of being knocked out. This is not the case."

Para-military riot police and demonstrators clashed for two consecutive nights in the streets of the capital Cayenne after police on Tuesday arrested Jean-Victor Castor and Fabien Canavy, both members of the Guiana Workers Union (UTG) which favours independence from France.
Jean-Claude Ringuet, a member of the pro-independence Guiana National Popular Party (PNPG), surrendered to police after taking refuge for several hours in Cayenne's town hall on Tuesday.
Officials said eight of the nine police injured overnight were hit by gunfire.
Local state-owned television said Castor, Canavy and Ringuet were taken to the French Caribbean island of Martinique aboard a French naval vessel on Thursday.
Lawyers for the detained men said they had received no official information on their clients' whereabouts and did not know where they were.

Unrest this month followed arrests including that of Alain Michel, a founding member of the PNPG. Michel was detained on April 11 and taken the next day with four others to Martinique aboard a military aircraft.

He was charged with arson and violence against a magistrate when the residence of French Guiana's state prosecutor was attacked last November during a previous wave of riots . In that wave of riots one person was killed and millions of dollars worth of property was damaged.
French officials at the time described the riots as "a deliberate attempt to destabilise French Guiana."

French Guiana, on the northeast coast of South America, is the only non-independent territory on the Western Hemisphere mainland. Its economy is heavily dependent on subsidies from France and 23 percent of the population of 150,000 is unemployed.
